bonus_mechanics: No personal income tax (Hall tax on interest and dividends repealed for periods beginning 1 Jan 2021). Entity level only: the 6.5% excise tax on LLCs, LPs, corporations and similar entities disallows federal bonus depreciation for assets purchased on or before 31 Dec 2022: add back all IRC 168 depreciation not permitted (Sch. J line 6 on the FAE174 form) and deduct the MACRS depreciation on the added-back basis in later years (lines 20/21).
change_note: Pub. Ch. 377 (2023) later coupled to TCJA bonus, only for assets purchased on or after 1 Jan 2023; it does not reach 2021.
special_rules: (1) Individuals file no Tennessee income tax return; the rule bites only where the business is an entity subject to franchise and excise tax (corporations, LPs, LLCs, business trusts per the agency page; sole proprietorships and general partnerships are not listed there). (2) Because bonus was disallowed, basis differs from federal: gain or loss on sale of such an asset is adjusted (Sch. J line 21). (3) 179 expensing is deducted to the same extent as on the federal return; partner-level 179 limits are disregarded and the entity applies the limit (FAE174 instructions Sch. J1 lines 2 and 5).

bonus_mechanics: No personal income tax. Entity level only: the franchise (margin) tax, report year 2022 for an accounting year ending in 2021, uses the IRC as of the federal tax year beginning 1 Jan 2007 for depreciation in cost of goods sold (COGS). Federal bonus depreciation is not allowed for Texas COGS: 'the Economic Stimulus Act of 2008, which introduced the current bonus depreciation rules, became part of the IRC after Jan. 1, 2007.' No add-back/subtract schedule: depreciation is simply computed as of the 2007 Code.
conformity_date: 2007-01-01 (IRC in effect for the federal tax year beginning on Jan. 1, 2007)
change_note: Not changed until the 2026 report year (accounting year 2025).
special_rules: (1) Depreciation only matters if the entity uses the COGS method and only for assets associated with and necessary for the production of goods (Tax Code 171.1012(c)(6)); entities using compensation, 70% of revenue or the USD 1 million deduction use no depreciation. (2) Sole proprietorships (except single-member LLCs) and general partnerships wholly owned by natural persons are not subject to franchise tax. (3) 179 under the 2007 IRC: limit 25,000 and phase-out threshold 200,000 per the Comptroller FAQ.

bonus_mechanics: No personal income tax. Franchise tax 2026 report (accounting year ending in 2025): the Comptroller now lets a COGS filer 'include in its COGS depreciation reported on its federal tax return to the extent associated with and necessary for the production of goods', including federal bonus depreciation and federal section 179, instead of the 2007 IRC. So it follows the federal return: 100% for property acquired after 19 Jan 2025, 40% for earlier 2025 acquisitions. An entity that claims bonus federally cannot opt out ('generally must use the same methods it uses on its current federal return').
conformity_date: Federal law in effect for the federal tax year, except where a Texas statute or rule references the IRC (those still use the 1 Jan 2007 Code)
change_note: Comptroller news release 1 Dec 2025 and Tax Policy memo (STAR 202512012M): from the 2026 report, depreciation follows current federal law. Rule 3.587 effective 1 Mar 2026; Rule 3.588 amendments adopted without change (filed 1 Jun 2026, effective 21 Jun 2026). This is an administrative position and rule change, not a change to the Tax Code.
special_rules: (1) One-time net depreciation adjustment on the 2026 report only: for each qualifying asset (placed in service before the accounting-year begin date on the 2026 report, not disposed of, and associated with and necessary for the production of goods), the difference between depreciation claimed federally and depreciation claimed for Texas COGS. The 2026 report is the only one on which it can be taken. Reported statements about whether unused amounts carry forward conflict between the proposed and adopted versions (see verify_note). (2) Only COGS filers use depreciation. (3) R&D under IRC 174 can still be elected under the 2007 Code method for COGS. (4) Sole proprietorships (except single-member LLCs) and natural-person general partnerships are not taxable entities.
source_citation: Texas Comptroller COGS FAQ (Beginning with the 2026 Report Year); IRC conformity FAQ https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/faq/irc-conformity.php ; Tax Policy News Jan 2026 https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/tax-policy-news/2026-january.php ; news release 1 Dec 2025 https://comptroller.texas.gov/about/media-center/news/20251201-acting-texas-comptroller-kelly-hancock-updates-franchise-tax-depreciation-rules-to-align-with-federal-provisions-1764005132713 ; 34 TAC 3.588(d)(6)(A)-(D) https://www.sos.state.tx.us/texreg/archive/June122026/Adopted%20Rules/34.PUBLIC%20FINANCE.html
verify_note: All of the above read at the agency pages and the Texas Register adoption notice on 2026-10-06 (fetch summaries, not the full text of the rule). 168(n) = false is inferred: no carve-out for qualified production property was found, and the rule says federal depreciation is included. 179 limit is the federal 2025 figure carried; Texas does not print it. Carryforward status of an unused one-time adjustment: the proposed-rule summary said unused amounts carry forward to consecutive reports; the adoption notice summary quotes the Comptroller as saying there is 'not a carryforward provision in COGS for unused costs'. Unresolved; read the rule text before relying on it.

bonus_mechanics: Vermont decouples from IRC 168(k) by statute: 32 V.S.A. 5811(21) 'Taxable income means federal taxable income determined without regard to Section 168(k) of the Internal Revenue Code'. In the year placed in service, add the federal depreciation (including bonus) minus normal MACRS depreciation (Schedule IN-112, Part I, Addition line 'Federal Bonus Depreciation'); in later years subtract the difference between federal depreciation and Vermont MACRS depreciation (the 'Adjustment for Bonus Depreciation on Prior Year Property' line). No spread: Vermont simply keeps a second, normal-MACRS depreciation schedule. Pass-through owners take their share from Schedule K-1VT.
change_note: Decoupling dates from 2002 (C corporations) and the individual disallowance from Act 190 of 2008 (TB-44); the Department says it applies for tax years 2008 and forward.
special_rules: (1) Bonus and 179 must be treated consistently at federal and state level: 'You cannot utilize the bonus depreciation for Federal purposes and use Section 179 for Vermont purposes' (TB-44). (2) On disposal, recompute gain or loss using Vermont depreciation: different Vermont and federal basis. (3) Nonresident partners/shareholders on IN-113 use the federal K-1 amounts before the bonus disallowance. (4) Vermont's IRC link-up is annual (statute adopts the Code as of a stated date), so the date for 2021 is not confirmed.
source_citation: Vermont Dept of Taxes Technical Bulletin TB-44 (issued 22 Jan 2009) https://tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/TB44.pdf ; Compliance Corner https://tax.vermont.gov/tax-law-and-guidance/compliance-corner ('Applicable Tax Years: 2008 and forward' per fetch summary)
verify_note: TB-44 text read in full 2026-10-06 (quotes 5811(21)); no 2021 instruction booklet was read (the 645 KB booklet was saved but not read in full), so the 2021 case rests on the standing statute plus the agency's '2008 and forward'. 179 limit and phase-out are federal figures carried as inherited. Conformity date for 2021 not confirmed.

bonus_mechanics: 2025 Schedule IN-112, line 4 (read in full): add the difference between standard MACRS and depreciation using the federal bonus for assets placed in service in 2025, including the OBBBA 100% bonus (Vermont continues to disregard 168(k)); pass-through owners add the part of K-1VT lines 8aA, 8bA and 38A for assets placed in service in 2025. Line 9 subtracts the difference for prior-year property.
conformity_date: 2025-12-31 (H. 933 / Act 164 of 2026, sec. 60 amending 32 V.S.A. 5824, effective for tax years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2025)
change_note: Act 164 (H. 933, 2026) retroactively conforms to P.L. 119-21 for tax years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2025 (agency page: 'retroactively applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025') but denies IRC 168(n) qualified production property expensing and IRC 174A R&E expensing for large businesses; also denies the section 250 deduction; adds back the 1202 exclusion from 2026.
special_rules: (1) 168(n) qualified production property: not allowed for Vermont; depreciation recomputed (inferred: under normal MACRS, as with 168(k)). (2) 179: conformity to the OBBBA 2,500,000/4,000,000 amounts is inferred from the 31 Dec 2025 link-up and the absence of a 179 decoupling in the agency's list of three affected areas; no Vermont page states the figures. (3) Amended 2025 returns: the Department offers penalty and interest relief for conformity changes; extended due date 15 Oct 2026. (4) The 2025 Federal Conformity Supplement to the instructions was not read.
